title: 401(K) WHEN YOU CHANGE JOBS: 6 THINGS TO KNOW
series_label: WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR 401(K) WHEN YOU CHANGE JOBS: 6 THINGS TO KNOW

concepts.title: Four Choices At Job Change
concepts.body: When you leave a job, your 401(k) goes one of four ways: (1) leave it in the old plan, (2) roll it to the new employer's plan, (3) roll it to a Rollover IRA, (4) cash out. Each has different tax, fee, and control consequences. Cash out is the worst in nearly every case.

concepts.title: The Cash-Out Tax Bomb
concepts.body: Cashing out a 401(k) at a younger job is brutally expensive. On $20,000 vested: 22% federal tax = $4,400, plus 10% early-withdrawal penalty = $2,000, plus state tax. Total: ~$6,400 gone — and you've lost the $20K's future growth. The leftover $13,600 is what you actually get.

concepts.title: The 60-Day Rollover Trap
concepts.body: If you do an indirect rollover, the old plan sends you a check and you have 60 days to deposit it into a new 401(k) or IRA. Miss the deadline and the whole amount is treated as a distribution — taxed plus 10% penalty. Worse: the old plan withholds 20% for taxes upfront, and you must replace that from your own pocket.

visual_spec.callout_text: Indirect rollover = 60-day deadline. Old plan withholds 20% upfront. Miss the deadline = full distribution + 10% penalty. Direct trustee-to-trustee transfer avoids both.

concepts.title: Auto-Rollovers (SECURE 2.0)
concepts.body: Starting in 2025, plans must auto-enroll departing employees with balances between $1,000 and $7,000 into a default IRA — unless you opt out. Under $1,000 gets force-paid as a check. Over $7,000 stays put. Auto-rolled balances must follow ERISA's safe-harbor rules.

concepts.title: Direct Rollovers: The Safe Move
concepts.body: Always do a trustee-to-trustee transfer: the old plan sends money straight to the new 401(k) or IRA, never to you. No 60-day clock, no 20% withholding, no tax event. Fill out the new plan's rollover form, give it to the old plan, and the money moves.

concepts.title: Pick By Situation
concepts.body: Old plan has good low-cost funds? Leave it. New employer's plan is generous? Roll in. Want full control and broad fund choice? Rollover IRA at Fidelity/Schwab/Vanguard. The one wrong answer for almost everyone: cash out. The one right answer for almost everyone: direct rollover.

visual_spec.callout_text: Default to a direct rollover. Old plan good? Leave it. New plan great? Roll in. Want control? Rollover IRA. Avoid cashing out in nearly every case.

sources_footer: Sourced from IRS Publication 575, U.S. Dept. of Labor Rollover notice, SECURE 2.0 Act Section 334, IRS 402(c) rollover rules
